data.gender_notes: Hill is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘heh’ meaning high and ‘hl’ meaning hill. The name Hill signifies elevation, height, or a mound. In the Bible, hills often represent spiritual elevation, as in the mountains where Moses received the Ten Commandments. The name Hill carries the meaning “Height, mound, or elevation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hill usually hope their child will grow to embody height, mound, or elevation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of spiritual elevation, connection to the divine.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hill total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hill has Anglo-Saxon origins and deeply resonates with the English language. In England, Hill is a common surname and toponym, meaning many places bear this name. It is also used colloquially to refer to prominent features in the landscape, adding to the rich historical and cultural associations.
data.spiritual_significance: In the context of Christianity, the name Hill holds spiritual significance as a symbol of spiritual elevation and ascension. In Holy Scripture, several biblical events occurred on hills, such as the miracle of the loaves and fishes on the Mount of the Beatitudes or the Mount of Transfiguration where Jesus revealed his divine nature. Thus, the name Hill serves as a reminder of the spiritual heights one can aspire to attain through faith and divine grace.
